description:
The British Columbia Institute of Technology is an educational institution in Vancouver, the capital city of British Columbia, that has been training experts, professionals and innovators to shape the economy since 1964. British Columbia Institute of Technology is founded on its educational strategy to go beyond textbooks and classrooms. BCIT students gain the technical skills, real-world experience and problem-solving ability necessary to lead innovation in the rapidly changing business world. Through close collaboration with industry, graduates achieve global success through the British Columbia Institute of Technology network. BCIT offers different program alternatives, from diplomas and certificates to undergraduate and graduate degrees.

BCIT main Campus is located on Willingdon Street in Burnaby City, next to Moscrop Secondary School and Deer Lake. It includes a library, gym and sports court, conference rooms, computer labs, and student services and administration offices. There is a Center for Applied Research and Innovation. Most of their full-time programs for the Faculty of Construction and Commerce, the Faculty of Business and the Faculty of Engineering are located on this campus.

The British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT) Aerospace Technology Campus is located near the Vancouver International Airport in Richmond. It offers aircraft maintenance engineering programs in aviation, maintenance, structures, aircraft gas turbine, overhaul training and repair, and aircraft mechanical component training programs.

In addition to commercial pilot training, BCIT also offers an airport operations training program for those wishing to pursue a career in airport management. Training takes place on the 285,000 square meter Aerospace Technology Campus, which opened in September 2007.

The RBC Foundation Aviation Library on the Aviation Technology Campus has one of the largest collections of aviation resources in Western Canada and has become a learning and study hub for aviation students, staff and the wider aviation industry in the region.
